meta.dataset: Punctual Pros public filings and regulatory data
meta.subject: Punctual Pros (f/k/a The Rohrer Company; East Hempfield Twp, Lancaster County PA); sponsor Broad Sky Partners (Fund I); add-on Horvath Home Services (Beachwood NJ)
meta.method: Pulled primary records directly: SEC EDGAR full-text search and Form D XML, SEC IAPD Form ADV PDF, USAspending.gov award API (SBA PPP/EIDL), Minnesota CARDS 2026 FDDs for One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky (Items 5-7, 19, 20 and franchisee exhibits), Lancaster County and NJOGIS parcel services, OSHA IMIS, BLS QCEW, plus press releases. Sites behind bot checks or CAPTCHAs (PA DOS, PA AG HIC, FederalPay, ProPublica, Wisconsin DFI, FDD aggregators) were not bypassed and are listed as data gaps. Category note: the PGIM 10-Q loan disclosure and the UGI proxy are tagged press_financial because the category list has no SEC-credit type.
meta.financial_picture: 1) Scale before the deal: The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll costs. At Lancaster's 2019 trade wage (~$62K) that is ~50-58 employees and roughly $9-12M of 2019 revenue (payroll at 30-40% of revenue); confidence medium. 2) Growth into the deal: headcount of ~113 by 2024 roughly doubles the PPP-implied base. At 2024 Lancaster wages of ~$76K and a 40-45% total labor ratio, that supports a PA revenue run-rate of ~$18-22M at the time of the BSP purchase. 3) FDD cross-check: the 2026 FDD franchisee lists show Punctual Pros operates 25 territories (PA: 9 One Hour, 7 Ben Franklin, 3 Mister Sparky; NJ: 3/2/1). Mapping those to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12-19M for PA and ~$3-5M for NJ in FY2025. Blending both methods, FY2025 pro forma revenue is estimated at ~$22M (range $16-28M), about $0.9M per territory, above system averages of $0.61-0.66M per territory for One Hour and Ben Franklin. 4) Franchise cost: royalty (6%) plus tiered brand fund (~1.2-1.5%) takes ~7.2-7.5% of revenue (~$1.6M a year), which caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8-14%. Estimated adjusted EBITDA is ~$1.8-3.1M (central ~$2.6M), confidence low. 5) Leverage: PGIM Private Credit Fund's 6/30/2026 10-Q discloses a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco, LLC at 3M SOFR+5.00% (8.73%), maturing 3/26/2029: $4.83M funded, fair value ~98.6% of par, plus a $1.4M unfunded delayed-draw commitment. This confirms a senior-secured, sponsor-style unitranche with an acquisition line. Total facility size is not disclosed; assuming PGIM-managed accounts hold most or all of it, total senior debt is plausibly ~$10-18M (~4-5.5x EBITDA, ~$0.9-1.6M of annual cash interest), confidence low. 6) Entry value: the undisclosed price, a lower-middle-market sell-side advisor (Boxwood) and no dedicated co-invest SPV (unlike Thomas Scientific, Frontline and CET) all point to an enterprise value probably in the ~$18-30M range and a Fund I equity check of roughly $8-15M, about 3-4% of the $335M fund; confidence low. 7) Growth drivers: 2025 same-store sales grew +8.4% (One Hour), +8.9% (Ben Franklin) and +14.3% (Mister Sparky) system-wide after a soft 2024. Punctual's PA territory count was flat, so growth is organic within existing territories plus the Horvath tuck-in (PPP-implied ~$3-4M 2019 revenue, 6 territories). 8) Demand signal: the user's deed dataset shows ~2,100 meaningful home sales per quarter inside the 248 modeled PA territory zips (~$574M priced volume in 90 days). That is a quantifiable new-mover lead pool, where a 5% capture rate means ~425 new relationships a year. 9) Clean profile: no OSHA inspections were found for Punctual/Rohrer/Horvath. The HQ property is held by a separate, likely related-party real-estate LLC (assessed $914.5K, recorded $1.5M sale), so rent is a normalization item. 10) Overall: the public record supports a ~$20-25M-revenue, ~$2-3M-EBITDA, moderately levered (4-5x) franchise-operator platform with a funded path for tuck-ins. Revenue ranges are medium confidence; EBITDA, debt and valuation are low confidence until confirmed by PitchBook or lender data.

data_gaps: No Form D exists for Punctual Pros, The Rohrer Company, Punctual Pros Midco or any Punctual-specific co-invest vehicle (EDGAR full-text and entity search). Punctual Pros appears to sit wholly in Broad Sky Partners, LP (Fund I).

Total size, structure (unitranche vs. first-lien plus revolver) and administrative agent of the Punctual Pros Midco credit facility are not disclosed. Only PGIM Private Credit Fund's slice is public, and it first appears at 6/30/2026 (absent at 12/31/2025), so the original 2024 holder list is unknown.

PPP jobs reported, lender name and forgiveness amount/date for Rohrer and Horvath are not in the USAspending record. FederalPay and ProPublica returned bot-protection (403) pages and were not bypassed, and the SBA FOIA CSV was not downloaded in this pass.
PA Department of State business search and UCC search (file.dos.pa.gov) returned a security-check page. Entity formation dates, officers and UCC-1 secured parties were not retrieved.

PA Attorney General Home Improvement Contractor search requires a Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA (not attempted). PA L&I licensing was not retrieved, and PA has no statewide HVAC/plumbing license (municipal licensing).

NJ business entity records for Horvath Home Services Inc / Punctual Pros NJ, LLC (NJ DORES is paid) and NJ HVACR/plumbing/electrical license numbers were not retrieved. The NJ parcel composite omits owner name.

Wisconsin DFI, California DFPI DocQNet and FDD aggregator sites (franchimp, fddexchange, franchisechatter) were blocked. Minnesota CARDS 2026 FDDs were used instead. Item 19 does not identify individual franchisees' revenue, so Punctual's quartile placement is inferred.
Capital Constellation/Wafra stake size in BSP is undisclosed and below Form ADV Schedule B reporting thresholds.

Lancaster County GIS shows a 2022-03-11 sale/deed date for 516 Running Pump Rd (deed ref 6669035, $1.5M), but no mortgage or lease memorandum was retrieved. 518 Running Pump Rd (PP Electric address) did not return a separate parcel.
DOL Wage & Hour enforcement (API key required), PACER federal litigation and Lancaster County Prothonotary civil dockets were not searched. Census CBP API now requires a key (BLS QCEW used instead).
'Broad Sky Networks LLC' in Capital Southwest filings is an unrelated company (false positive).
User deed dataset: prices are 0 for Ocean, Chester, York and Monmouth; York rows lack dates; zip is blank for many non-Lancaster records, so territory counts understate true volume.
Sibling research (bsp_firm.json) notes BSP lists 2 Punctual Pros add-ons, but only Horvath is identified publicly.
next_pulls: PitchBook / Capital IQ deal profile for Broad Sky-Punctual Pros (2024-04-03): disclosed EV, revenue/EBITDA at entry, debt amount, lender list; also the second add-on name and date.

PitchBook LCD / Debtwire / 9fin / Private Credit data (e.g., Lincoln, Houlihan valuation marks): full Punctual Pros Midco facility size, agent, revolver and DDTL sizing, pricing history and marks across all PGIM and other BDC holders.
SBA PPP FOIA CSV (public_150k_plus, free from SBA): JobsReported, lender (ServicingLenderName), ForgivenessAmount/Date for Rohrer and Horvath.
PA DOS business and UCC search (manual browser session): formation dates for Punctual Pros Midco, PP OH/Plumbing/Electric LLCs; UCC-1 secured party (agent) and filing date, likely 2024-03/04.
Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds (Landex) instrument 6669035 and any memorandum of lease or mortgage on 516/518 Running Pump Rd; Ocean County Clerk for 1130 Ship Ave ownership and liens.
Minnesota CARDS 2023-2025 FDDs for the three brands: multi-year Item 19 trend to back-test PA territory revenue, and Item 21 audited franchisor financials (royalty revenue by brand).
ZoomInfo / LinkedIn Talent Insights / Dun & Bradstreet: current headcount, technician count and revenue estimates for Punctual Pros and Horvath.

ServiceTitan / Nexstar / ACCA benchmark reports (paid or member): average ticket, close rate, membership attach and EBITDA margin for $15-30M residential HVAC/plumbing operators, to replace assumed 8-14% margin.
PACER and Lancaster/Ocean County civil dockets; DOL WHD enforcement data (enforcedata.dol.gov with API key).
Backfill price and zip on the Ocean, Chester, York and Monmouth deed records (e.g., ATTOM or county API) so the new-mover marketing layer covers the NJ Horvath territory with priced sales.

items.entity: Broad Sky Partners, LP (Fund I; CIK 0001917706)
items.title: Form D (original): Broad Sky Partners, LP pooled private equity fund offering
items.filer_or_source_agency: U.S. SEC (EDGAR), filed by Broad Sky Partners, LP
items.what_it_tells_us: Fund I had ~$299M of commitments from only 14 investors at first close, a concentrated LP base typical of a first-time spin-out fund anchored by a few large institutions. This is the fund that bought Punctual Pros in April 2024. At this size, a single platform equity check is usually $20-60M, which means Punctual Pros (a smaller residential-services platform) was probably one of the smaller positions.

items.filer_or_source_agency: U.S. SEC (EDGAR)
items.what_it_tells_us: Commitments grew only ~$5M in the year after first close, so Fund I was essentially fully raised by early 2023. That was before the Punctual Pros deal.

items.entity: Broad Sky Partners, LP (Fund I; CIK 0001917706)
items.title: Form D/A (2024 annual amendment), signed about two weeks after the Punctual Pros closing
items.filer_or_source_agency: U.S. SEC (EDGAR)
items.what_it_tells_us: Fund I commitments rose $20.04M year over year to $323.8M. That is consistent with a late commitment or a GP top-up and does not by itself tie to the Punctual Pros check. The filing confirms the fund had capital available for the April 3, 2024 acquisition without a new vehicle.

items.title: Form D/A (2025 annual amendment): Broad Sky Partners, LP
items.filer_or_source_agency: U.S. SEC (EDGAR)
items.what_it_tells_us: Fund I closed its offering at $335M. The jump from 16 to 46 counted investors most likely reflects feeder or employee participants, not new large LPs. Punctual Pros sits in a sub-$350M fund, so it matters to BSP's returns and add-on M&A there will be closely watched.

items.what_it_tells_us: BSP raised dedicated co-invest SPVs for Thomas Scientific (~$365M across vehicles), Frontline (~$167M) and CET ($7.5M) but none for Punctual Pros. That points to Punctual Pros being funded entirely from Fund I, with an equity check small enough not to need LP co-invest. Relative to the TS and FL SPVs, the Punctual Pros equity check was probably well under $50M.

items.what_it_tells_us: This is the only public filing that reveals Punctual Pros' LBO debt. The borrower is a 'Midco' holding entity, the loan is senior secured unitranche/first-lien at S+500, and the 3/26/2029 maturity implies a 5-year loan dated at the April 2024 closing. Fair value at ~98.6% of par (cost ~98.6%) shows the credit is performing. The $1.4M undrawn DDTL (PGIM PCF's share only) is a committed add-on acquisition facility. Total facility size and agent are not disclosed. PGIM PCF's $4.83M is probably a slice of a larger PGIM-managed allocation across affiliated accounts.

items.what_it_tells_us: Punctual Pros' PP OH, LLC holds 9 PA One Hour territories, roughly the size of a top-quartile franchisee (172 territories / 22 = 7.8 each). That implies FY2025 One Hour revenue in the ~$4.4M (quartile floor) to ~$11.5M (quartile average) range, with ~$7.4M as the central case. Plus ~$1-3M for the 3 NJ One Hour territories. System same-store growth of +8.4% in 2025 after a -6.6% 2024 is a tailwind for 2025-26 marks.

key_figures.per_unit_goal: grow franchise brands that average over $1 million in per-unit revenue

items.what_it_tells_us: Punctual Pros is a multi-brand operator inside a $2B+ system. Its likely ~$0.9M revenue per territory (about $22M over 25 territories) is close to Authority's '$1M per unit' aspiration and above the One Hour and Ben Franklin system averages ($0.61M and $0.66M per territory).

items.entity: Plumbing/HVAC and electrical contractors (NAICS 23822, 23821), Lancaster County PA and Ocean County NJ
items.title: BLS QCEW private-sector employment and average annual pay, 2019 and 2024
items.filer_or_source_agency: U.S. BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (open data API)
items.what_it_tells_us: Lancaster plumbing/HVAC wages rose ~22.5% from 2019 to 2024, which squeezes margins at a royalty-paying franchisee. At ~$76K average pay, ~113 PA employees imply ~$8.6M of wages (~$9.5-10M with benefits and taxes), which supports a PA revenue run-rate near $20M at a 40-45% total labor ratio. With ~2,847 plumbing/HVAC workers in Lancaster County, Punctual Pros (~100 there) holds roughly a 3-4% labor share, so it is local scale but not dominant.

items.entity: Residential deed transfers in Punctual Pros' counties (PA: Lancaster, Dauphin, Chester, York, Montgomery; NJ: Ocean, Monmouth)
items.title: 90-day county recorder deed-transfer pull as a new-mover demand and marketing signal (user-compiled dataset)
items.filer_or_source_agency: County recorders of deeds (compiled in /Users/syed/BSP/data/pp_sales_90d.json; territory from pp_zips.json)

key_figures.data_quality: prices missing (0) for Ocean, Chester, York, Monmouth; York rows lack dates

items.what_it_tells_us: The 248 modeled PA territory zips see ~2,100 meaningful sales per quarter (~8,500 a year). Each is a new owner who typically has inspection-driven HVAC, water-heater, panel and plumbing work in the first 12-24 months. Capturing 5% would add ~425 new customer relationships a year, meaningful against a ~$22M revenue base, and would make the deed feed a practical marketing portal. Ocean County, where Horvath operates, shows the heaviest transfer volume (3,190 in 90 days), so it deserves priority targeting once price and zip fields are backfilled.
